function.mechanism: Metallic silver flakes/particles reflect light and create a lustrous silver appearance on food surfaces.
common_food_categories: Decorative use in some liqueur applications

adi.basis: EFSA 2016 reported no numerical ADI could be established; EFSA 2025 follow-up could not conclude on safety due inadequate data.

efsa.key_finding: Latest EFSA follow-up (2025) concluded that submitted data were inadequate and safety of E174 could not be concluded; nanoscale risk assessment is required.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 73.2500 (cosmetics); no silver GRAS listing found in 21 CFR Parts 182/184 for food use

adi.basis: JECFA silver record shows ADI outcome as decision postponed (1977); 2018 entry notes not re-evaluated and provisions withdrawn at CCFA50.

concerns.summary: EFSA follow-up reported that submitted genotoxicity evidence for E174 was inadequate for a safety conclusion.
Reviews of nanoparticle food additives including E174 report oral-exposure associations with gastrointestinal and microbiota-related effects and oxidative-stress-mediated toxicity hypotheses.
Material-characterization studies on market E174 and decorated products found substantial nanoparticle fractions and release of silver nanoparticles from pastry decoration materials.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI is available, so conventional ADI exceedance cannot be quantified; EFSA identified unresolved uncertainty and could not conclude safety in 2025.

risk_assessment.rationale: Latest EFSA assessment was unable to conclude safety, with unresolved particle characterization and toxicology gaps, and no numerical ADI available for routine margin-based risk management.
key_factors: EFSA 2016: no numerical ADI could be established
EFSA 2025: unable to conclude on safety of E174
Evidence of nanoparticle fractions/release in E174-containing products
JECFA silver record lacks a positive ADI allocation and notes withdrawn provisions context
No U.S. food GRAS listing identified in CFR Parts 182/184
